result.title: Aligning, Fast and Slow: A Control-Theoretic Oversight Framework for Long-Horizon Trajectories and Maintained Deployments
result.summary: AI agents can pass checks on individual tasks while retaining memory or code changes that alter their later behavior. We introduce a control-theoretic framework that couples a fast loop controlling proposed actions with a slow loop reviewing persistent changes and reassessing configurations after model or tool updates. When measurement errors and changes between checks are bounded and controllers can enforce their decisions, we derive a deployment-level bound and a rule for dividing review effort. In simulation, dividing a fixed review budget between both loops reduces mean maximum departure from intended behavior roughly twelvefold compared with review confined to individual runs. In coding stress tests with authored memories and five matched seeds, combined controls reduce mean severity on a 0-3 scale from 0.325 without gates to 0.117, resolving 33 of 120 issues versus 35 without gates; in trading stress tests, combined controls reduce mean shortfall in low-emission purchases from 0.892 without gates to 0.107. The overall framework helps developers and auditors compare and enforce oversight designs, while the agent studies test component controls rather than the full deployment-level guarantee.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个控制论式监督框架：快速回路审查每步提出的动作，慢速回路定期复核持久性改动（记忆、代码）并在模型或工具更新后重评配置，并给出部署层面的偏差界与审查预算分配规则，用编码与交易压力测试验证组合控制的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「快回路/慢回路」分工与固定审查预算如何在两者间切分，可能与 LVR 中 THINK 步数、视觉证据复核与停止决策之间的计算分配问题形成类比，可供核查；但该文不涉及多模态内部表示，联系仅为概念层面。
